Declared primary credential (SHERPADESK_API_KEY) and python runtime requirements align with the repository contents and documented functionality. No unrelated cloud credentials or unexpected external services are requested.

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md explicitly instructs creating workspace-local state under .SherpaMind/, staging the SherpaDesk API key there, running CLI commands (python3 scripts/run.py ...), bootstrapping a venv, and optionally installing a user-level systemd service. Those actions are within the stated scope (ingest, sync, materialize artifacts, run background sync). The instructions do ask the agent to read/write files under the workspace and to stage secrets locally—this is intentional for a local backend.

Installing packages from PyPI and creating a local venv is expected for a Python backend, but users should note that runtime bootstrap will fetch external packages (httpx, pydantic, etc.).

The skill stores the staged API key in a local file (.SherpaMind/secrets/sherpadesk_api_key.txt) by design; storing secrets on disk is proportional to offline local sync but is a security decision the operator should accept (see guidance). Other environment variables mentioned are optional controls, not required secrets.

llm.guidance: This skill appears to be what it says: a local SherpaDesk backend plus OpenClaw guidance. Before installing or bootstrapping, consider: (1) you will need to provide a SherpaDesk API key; the tool will stage it under .SherpaMind/secrets (rotate the key if you later remove the skill). (2) The bootstrap process creates a Python venv and installs packages from PyPI—review requirements and ensure you trust those dependencies. (3) The optional background service is a user-level systemd unit (no system-wide privilege required) but gives the skill persistent background behavior—only install it if you want ongoing sync. (4) Review scripts/run.py and scripts/bootstrap.py (and the repository tests) locally before running; run doctor/bootstrap-audit first to see what will be created. (5) Keep the workspace location under your control and ensure .SherpaMind/ is placed where you accept local data storage. If you need higher assurance, run the bootstrap in an isolated environment, inspect the code paths that write .SherpaMind/secrets, and verify network calls are only to SherpaDesk (api.sherpadesk.com) and the project GitHub as expected.
